result.text:
801:  \le\exp(u^2\sigma^2/2).
802: \end{equation}
803: Thus the noise condition is imposed after the action is selected and before
804: the reward is revealed.  The ridge penalty is centered at zero in the chosen
805: parameter coordinates, and every norm bound below, including
806: $\|\btheta^\circ\|_2\le S$, uses those coordinates.  For a pretrained
807: initialization $\btheta_0$, the intended convention is displacement coordinates
808: $\btheta=\btheta_{\rm orig}-\btheta_0$; then $S$ bounds the displacement of the
809: reference model from initialization rather than its raw parameter norm.  Fix
810: before data collection a reference parameter $\btheta^\circ\in\Theta$ with
811: $\|\btheta^\circ\|_2\le S$, and allow
812: approximate realizability
813: \begin{equation}\label{eq:approx-realizability-new}
814:  \mu^*(z)=\mu_{\btheta^\circ}(z)+m^\circ(z),\qquad
815:  |m^\circ(z)|\le\epsilon_{\rm mis}(z).
816: \end{equation}
817: \paragraph{Turn past rewards into a frozen linear estimation problem.}
818: The predictable sequence $\btheta_t\in\Theta$ is otherwise arbitrary.  Set
819: $\bq_t(a)=\nabla_\theta\mu_{\btheta_t}(x_t,a)$.  A collection-time
820: linearization has a known nonlinear offset and a linear term in the reference
821: parameter.  Subtracting that offset from the reward gives a
822: \emph{pseudo-response}: an approximate linear observation of the fixed
823: reference parameter, with noise and Taylor and misspecification errors.
824: The pseudo-responses and their frozen ridge estimate are
825: \begin{align}
826:  y_s&=r_s-\mu_{\btheta_s}(x_s,a_s)+\bq_s(a_s)^\top\btheta_s,
827:  \label{eq:pseudo-response-new}\\
828:  \hat\btheta_t^{\rm lin}
829:  &=\bVbar_t^{-1}\sigma^{-2}\sum_{s<t}\bq_s(a_s)y_s.
830:  \label{eq:frozen-ridge-new}
831: \end{align}
832: \paragraph{Correct the current prediction.}
833: The linear estimate uses old, predictable features, while the action query
834: uses the current model.  The corrected center connects them:
835: \begin{equation}\label{eq:corrected-center-new}
836:  m_t^{\rm corr}(a)=\mu_{\btheta_t}(x_t,a)
837:  +\bq_t(a)^\top(\hat\btheta_t^{\rm lin}-\btheta_t).
838: \end{equation}
839: 
840: The correction applies the current gradient to the difference between the
841: frozen linear estimate and the current parameter.  Thus the certified center
842: is generally different from the raw prediction of the trained model.  The
843: identity supporting its confidence band holds for any predictable parameter
844: path in the certified region, but it does not make the approximation errors
845: small.
846: 
847: \paragraph{Account for historical and current errors separately.}
848: Fix $\delta\in(0,1)$.  Let $\rho_s^\circ$ be the Taylor remainder of
849: $\mu_{\btheta^\circ}$ around $\btheta_s$, and supply envelopes
850: \begin{equation}\label{eq:lin-mis-envelopes-new}
851:  |\rho_s^\circ|\le\epsilon_{\rm lin}(s),\qquad
852:  |m^\circ(x_s,a_s)|\le\epsilon_{\rm mis}(s),
853: \end{equation}
854: with the corresponding actionwise current envelopes
855: $\epsilon_{\rm lin,t}(a)$ and $\epsilon_{\rm mis,t}(a)$.  Each envelope is
856: deterministic or measurable before the reward at the round where it is used;
857: the complete historical sum below is known before selecting $a_t$.
858: Past errors affect the fitted linear estimate and therefore enlarge the
859: confidence radius.  Current errors enter the final prediction band
860: additively.  Define
861: \begin{equation}\label{eq:beta-corrected-new}
862:  \begin{aligned}
863:   \beta_t^{\rm corr}
864:   &=\sqrt{\gamma_{t-1}+2\log(1/\delta)}+\sqrt\lambda S\\
865:   &\quad+\frac1\sigma\sqrt{\sum_{s<t}
866:   [\epsilon_{\rm lin}(s)+\epsilon_{\rm mis}(s)]^2}.
867:  \end{aligned}
868: \end{equation}
869: 
870: The radius contains the stochastic uncertainty term, the ridge penalty for
871: the reference parameter, and the accumulated historical approximation error.
872: The following result supplies the reference-confidence band required by
873: \Cref{asm:abstract-transport}.
874: 
875: \begin{corollary}[Corrected-center confidence without optimizer assumptions]
876: \label{cor:corrected-center-new}
877: With probability at least $1-\delta$, simultaneously over rounds and actions,
878: \begin{equation}\label{eq:corrected-confidence-new}
879:  |\mu_t^*(a)-m_t^{\rm corr}(a)|
880:  \le\beta_t^{\rm corr}\bar s_t(a)
881:  +\epsilon_{\rm lin,t}(a)+\epsilon_{\rm mis,t}(a).
882: \end{equation}
883: The identity and bound hold for any predictable $\btheta_t$ in the certified
884: region.  They require no exact ERM, approximate stationarity, optimizer
885: residual, or optimizer convergence rate.
886: \end{corollary}
887: 
888: The historical deterministic term in \eqref{eq:beta-corrected-new} follows from
889: $\Phi_t^\top\bVbar_t^{-1}\Phi_t\preceq I$ for
890: $\Phi_t=[\bq_1/\sigma,\ldots,\bq_{t-1}/\sigma]$.  Its scaling is
891: $1/\sigma$, not $1/\sigma^2$.  Fixed nonvanishing misspecification generally
892: creates a linear current-bias term and can also make the historical radius
893: vacuous.  This is a graceful-degradation statement, not a robust
894: misspecified-bandit guarantee.
895: 
896: \section{When the regret bound is informative}
897: \label{sec:closed-rates-new}
898: 
899: The general theorem depends on quantities accumulated along the policy's
900: history.  This section replaces the information gain by a bound in terms of
901: parameter dimension and horizon, then asks when the remaining transport and
902: approximation terms are controlled.  A valid certificate alone is not enough:
903: a large historical error radius or persistent current bias can still prevent
904: the displayed regret bound from being sublinear.
905: 
906: \paragraph{Bound information gain using dimension.}
907: Let $r_T=\min\{d,T\}$.  The frozen Gram matrix has at most this rank above
908: its ridge term.  Bounding its eigenvalue sum using the query-norm bound gives
909: \begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-d-gamma-new}
910:  \gamma_T\le\Gamma_{T,d}:=
911:  r_T\log\!\left(1+\frac{TG^2}{r_T\lambda\sigma^2}\right).
912: \end{equation}
913: No fixed tangent subspace is required.  The next corollary substitutes this
914: bound and the corrected-center radius into the general theorem.  Its
915: $B_T$ collects historical error energy, while $E_T^{\rm cur}$ collects the
916: current prediction-error allowances.
917: 
918: \begin{corollary}[Finite-dimensional corrected-center rate]
919: \label{cor:finite-d-rate-new}
920: Suppose $\bar D_t\le D$, $\alpha_t\le\alpha$, and
921: $\kappa_{+,t}/\kappa_{-,t}\le K$ for all $t$.  Let
922: \begin{align*}
923:  B_T&=\sum_{s<T}[\epsilon_{\rm lin}(s)+\epsilon_{\rm mis}(s)]^2,\\
924:  E_T^{\rm cur}&=\sum_{t=1}^T
925:  [\epsilon_{\rm lin,t}(a_t)+\epsilon_{\rm mis,t}(a_t)].
926: \end{align*}
927: Then \Cref{thm:transported-ucb,cor:corrected-center-new} imply
928: \begin{align}
929: R_T
930: &\le2\alpha e^D\sqrt K\nonumber\\
931: &\quad{}\times
932: \left[\sqrt{\Gamma_{T,d}+2\log(1/\delta)}+\sqrt\lambda S
933: +\frac{\sqrt{B_T}}{\sigma}\right]\nonumber\\
934: &\quad{}\times
935: \sqrt{\left(\sigma^2+\frac{G^2}{\lambda}\right)T\Gamma_{T,d}}
936: \nonumber\\
937: &\quad+2E_T^{\rm cur}+\sum_{t=1}^T\xi_t.
938: \label{eq:finite-d-rate-new-display}
939: \end{align}
940: With exact realizability and a frozen linear model, $B_T=E_T^{\rm cur}=0$.
941: For fixed $d$ and problem constants, the leading term is then
942: $O(e^D\sqrt K\,d\sqrt T\log T)$.  Exact solves set $\alpha=1$, exact current
943: curvature sets $K=1$, and exact score maximization sets $\xi_t=0$, recovering
944: the standard LinUCB determinant-potential rate up to displayed constants.
945: \end{corollary}
946: 
947: \paragraph{Control both transport and linearization error.}
948: The preceding bound becomes useful when the transport factors stay controlled
949: and the approximation errors are small enough.  The next corollary gives a
950: sufficient regime: the model is nearly linear throughout a certified parameter
951: region.  Its scale $W$ controls both gradient change and Taylor error.  The
952: condition relates this scale to the horizon; it is not a statement that an
953: arbitrary fixed nonlinear model has sublinear regret.
954: 
955: \begin{corollary}[Global near-linearity under exponential transport]
956: \label{cor:global-near-linear-new}
957: Assume exact realizability, $\mu^*(z)=\mu_{\btheta^\circ}(z)$, and suppose
958: $\|\btheta^\circ\|_2\le R$ and $\|\btheta_t\|_2\le R$ for every $t$.
959: On the certified convex radius-$R$ region, assume the prediction gradient is
960: $L_\mu$-Lipschitz for the Taylor envelopes and satisfies the replay-path
961: Hessian bound $L_g$ in \Cref{cor:hessian-path-new}, with
962: \[
963:  L_\mu\le\frac{c_\mu}{\sqrt W},\qquad
964:  L_g\le\frac{c_g}{\sqrt W},
965: \]
966: with $W>0$.  Use the corrected center, exact current curvature, exact dense
967: solves, and exact score maximization in finite parameter dimension $d$, and
968: suppose $\|\bq_t(a)\|_2\le G$.  Thus
969: $\alpha_t=1$, $\kappa_{-,t}=\kappa_{+,t}=1$, and $\xi_t=0$.
970: Define
971: \[
972:  D_{T,W}:=\frac{4c_gR\sqrt{T-1}}{\sigma\sqrt{\lambda W}}.
973: \]
974: Then, with probability at least $1-\delta$,
975: \begin{align}
976:  R_T
977:  &\le 2e^{D_{T,W}}
978:  \Biggl[
979:  \begin{aligned}
980:   &\sqrt{\Gamma_{T,d}+2\log(1/\delta)}+\sqrt\lambda R\\[-1mm]
981:   &\quad+\frac{2c_\mu R^2\sqrt T}{\sigma\sqrt W}
982:  \end{aligned}
983:  \Biggr]\nonumber\\[-1mm]
984:  &\quad\times
985:  \sqrt{\sigma^2+\frac{G^2}{\lambda}}\,
986:  \sqrt{T\Gamma_{T,d}}\nonumber\\
987:  &\quad+\frac{4c_\mu R^2T}{\sqrt W}.
988:  \label{eq:global-near-linear-new}
989: \end{align}
990: Consequently, $W=\Omega(T)$ with a sufficiently large problem-dependent
991: constant keeps $D_{T,W}=O(1)$.  For fixed $d$ and fixed problem constants,
992: \[
993:  R_T=O(d\sqrt T\log T)+O(\sqrt T).
994: \]
995: This conclusion requires no $D_t<1$ condition.  Here $W$ is an abstract
996: near-linearity scale, not generic network width or parameter count, and the
997: result is not an unrestricted neural-training theorem.  No optimizer-residual
998: rate is required because the corrected center is used.
999: \end{corollary}
1000: 
1001: \begin{remark}[Comparable guarantees do not order policies]
1002: \Cref{prop:frozen-width-ucb,cor:corrected-center-new} give a frozen-width
1003: counterpart to \eqref{eq:finite-d-rate-new-display}, with the factor
1004: $\alpha e^D\sqrt K$ removed and all remaining quantities evaluated on the
1005: frozen policy's own history.  With the same $\lambda$, $\sigma$, and
1006: confidence level, common uniform bounds on the query norm, reference norm,
1007: approximation envelopes, and accumulated oracle error give guarantees of the
1008: same order when $D$, $\alpha$, and $K$ are bounded.  In particular, under the
1009: statistical, uniform-region, and smoothness assumptions of
1010: \Cref{cor:global-near-linear-new}, the corrected center and exact
1011: frozen-width score maximization give the same
1012: $O(d\sqrt T\log T)+O(\sqrt T)$ rate when $W=\Omega(T)$, for fixed $d$
1013: and fixed problem constants.
1014: This comparison does not rank realized regret: different selected actions
1015: change the representation paths, centers, radii, and information gains.
1016: It neither proves that transport is unnecessary nor rules out improved
1017: performance from current curvature.  The stated $W$ scaling is a sufficient
1018: condition for these bounds, not a necessary condition for an informative
1019: transport certificate.
1020: \end{remark}
1021: 
1022: \paragraph{A concrete model with fixed feature directions.}
1023: The scaled-tanh model makes the smoothness condition explicit.  It also has
1024: more structure than the general Hessian argument uses: changing the parameter
1025: rescales each feature gradient without rotating its direction.  This permits
1026: the sharper endpoint comparison developed after the model's derivative
1027: formulas.
1028: 
1029: \begin{remark}[Scaled-tanh specialization]
1030: For
1031: \[
1032:  \mu_{\btheta,W}(z)=\sqrt W\tanh\!\left(
1033:  \frac{\phi(z)^\top\btheta}{\sqrt W}\right),
1034:  \qquad \|\phi(z)\|_2\le B_\phi,
1035: \]
1036: write $u=\phi(z)^\top\btheta/\sqrt W$.  Then
1037: \begin{align*}
1038:  \nabla_\theta\mu_{\btheta,W}(z)
1039:  &=\operatorname{sech}^2(u)\phi(z),\\
1040:  \nabla_\theta^2\mu_{\btheta,W}(z)
1041:  &=-\frac{2}{\sqrt W}\operatorname{sech}^2(u)\tanh(u)
1042:  \phi(z)\phi(z)^\top.
1043: \end{align*}
1044: Since
1045: $\sup_u|2\operatorname{sech}^2(u)\tanh(u)|=4/(3\sqrt3)$,
1046: \Cref{cor:global-near-linear-new} applies with
1047: \[
1048:  G=B_\phi,\qquad
1049:  c_\mu=c_g=c_h:=\frac{4B_\phi^2}{3\sqrt3}.
1050: \]
1051: The symbol $W$ is a smoothness scale here; it is not identified with hidden
1052: width or parameter count.
1053: \end{remark}
1054: 
1055: \paragraph{Compare scalar weights instead of accumulating a path bound.}
1056: For a fixed observation, the gradients at collection time and at the current
1057: parameter point in the same feature direction.  Their contributions to the
1058: Gram matrix differ only by the \emph{squares} of their scalar gradient
1059: multipliers.  Bounds on the ratio of these weights therefore compare the
1060: endpoint matrices directly.  The common ridge term must be included in that
1061: comparison as well.
1062: 
1063: There are two versions.  A uniform bound uses only the parameter and feature
1064: norm bounds.  When observations share a finite collection of feature vectors,
1065: a category-wise bound uses the accumulated collection-time weight and the
1066: current weight within each category.  Both are certificates for the same
1067: reference-confidence construction; neither supplies a new statistical event.
1068: 
1069: \begin{corollary}[Relative weights for scaled tanh]
1070: \label{cor:tanh-relative-weights}
1071: For the scaled-tanh model above, suppose $W>0$, $\|\phi(z_s)\|_2\le B_\phi$,
1072: and $\|\btheta_s\|_2,\|\btheta_t\|_2\le R$ for all $s<t$.
1073: Set $\omega_\theta(z)=\operatorname{sech}^2(\phi(z)^\top\theta/\sqrt W)$ and
1074: $\ell=\operatorname{sech}^2(B_\phi R/\sqrt W)>0$.  For
1075: \begin{align*}
1076:  \bVbar_t&=\lambda\bI+\sigma^{-2}\sum_{s<t}
1077:  \omega_{\btheta_s}(z_s)^2\phi(z_s)\phi(z_s)^\top,\\
1078:  \bV_t&=\lambda\bI+\sigma^{-2}\sum_{s<t}
1079:  \omega_{\btheta_t}(z_s)^2\phi(z_s)\phi(z_s)^\top,
1080: \end{align*}
1081: the uniform endpoint certificate is
1082: \begin{equation}\label{eq:tanh-uniform-relative}
1083:  \ell^2\bVbar_t\preceq\bV_t\preceq\ell^{-2}\bVbar_t,
1084:  \qquad d_{\rm Th}(\bVbar_t,\bV_t)
1085:  \le4\log\cosh(B_\phi R/\sqrt W).
1086: \end{equation}
1087: If the observed feature vectors belong to a finite set $\{\phi_c\}$, let
1088: $n_{t,c}$ be their counts, let
1089: $f_{t,c}=\sum_{s<t:\phi(z_s)=\phi_c}\omega_{\btheta_s}(z_s)^2$, and put
1090: $g_{t,c}=n_{t,c}\operatorname{sech}^4(\phi_c^\top\btheta_t/\sqrt W)$.
1091: The sharper category certificate is
1092: \begin{equation}\label{eq:tanh-category-relative}
1093:  c_{-,t}=\min\!\left\{1,\min_{c:n_{t,c}>0}\frac{g_{t,c}}{f_{t,c}}\right\},
1094:  \qquad
1095:  c_{+,t}=\max\!\left\{1,\max_{c:n_{t,c}>0}\frac{g_{t,c}}{f_{t,c}}\right\},
1096: \end{equation}
1097: with $c_{-,1}=c_{+,1}=1$ for an empty history.  It satisfies
1098: \eqref{eq:relative-endpoint-sandwich} and
1099: $\ell^2\le c_{-,t}\le1\le c_{+,t}\le\ell^{-2}$.
1100: Either certificate can be used in \Cref{cor:relative-endpoint-ucb}.
1101: \end{corollary}
1102: 
1103: The uniform bound has no explicit horizon dependence when its norm bounds and
1104: $W$ are fixed.  This controls transport, but does not remove the separate
1105: historical and current approximation errors from the regret bound.
1106: For the category version, maintaining a count and a collection-weight sum
1107: per category lets \eqref{eq:tanh-category-relative} use current category
1108: projections without an eigensolve or a scan of the full history.  It reduces
1109: the work needed for this certificate, not the cost of all width or center
1110: solves.  The construction relies on fixed gradient directions and does not
1111: cover general gradient rotation or establish improved policy regret.
1112: The appendix gives the termwise proof and an example where the endpoint
1113: distance is zero although the synthetic path has positive length.
1114: 
1115: \paragraph{A local comparison when changes are small.}
1116: A local two-sided comparison gives another way to relate the same matrices.
1117: It replaces the exponential factors by a local sandwich that requires a
1118: smallness condition.
1119: If $\chi_t<1$ and
1120: \begin{equation}\label{eq:local-additive-new}
1121:  (1-\chi_t)^2\bVbar_t\preceq\bV_t
1122:  \preceq(1+\chi_t)^2\bVbar_t,
1123: \end{equation}
1124: use the local score obtained from \eqref{eq:transported-score-new} by replacing
1125: $e^{\bar D_t/2}$ with $1+\chi_t$.
1126: \begin{corollary}[Local small-drift transport]
1127: \label{cor:local-small-drift-new}
1128: Under the remaining hypotheses of \Cref{thm:transported-ucb}, the local score
1129: satisfies
1130: \begin{align}
1131: R_T
1132: &\le\sqrt{\left(\sigma^2+\frac{G^2}{\lambda}\right)\gamma_T
1133: \sum_{t=1}^T\beta_t^2
1134: \left[1+\alpha_t\frac{1+\chi_t}{1-\chi_t}
1135: \sqrt{\frac{\kappa_{+,t}}{\kappa_{-,t}}}\right]^2}
1136: \nonumber\\
1137: &\quad+2\sum_{t=1}^Tb_t(a_t)+\sum_{t=1}^T\xi_t.
1138: \label{eq:local-small-drift-regret-new}
1139: \end{align}
1140: \end{corollary}
1141: Neither the local factor nor the exponential factor uniformly dominates the
1142: other because they summarize different paths.

1173: \paragraph{What remains model-specific.}
1174: The geometric comparisons can be reused with another estimator if it supplies
1175: \eqref{eq:abstract-confidence-new}.  Geometry alone does not supply that
1176: statistical premise.  For an exponential-family model, one would also need a
1177: likelihood-score confidence event, a conversion to prediction error,
1178: pre-reward collection-time Fisher weights, control of weight and Jacobian
1179: transport, and an information-potential bound.  Those additional steps are
1180: outside the squared-loss specialization established here.
